CHOICE: 1
CONFIDENCE: 3

Solution 1's count is correct. In $K^q_{\lceil n/2\rceil,\lfloor n/2\rfloor}$, every triangle has the form $\{u_i,v_i,w\}$ with $w$ in the other part, and only vertices in the other part can be bowtie centers. Each such vertex is the center of $\binom{q}{2}$ bowties, giving $\lfloor n/2\rfloor\binom{q}{2}$ in total.

Solutions 2 and 3 are wrong because they ignore cross-triangles. A B-edge and an A-edge create many bowties together, which adds a term of order $n q_A q_B$. Their split configurations therefore have more bowties than they estimate. Their claim that the split preserves the spectral radius is also doubtful, since the first-order gains per edge differ ($1/a$ versus $1/b$).

The remaining uncertainty is whether some other graph with $\lambda(G)\ge\lambda(K^q)$ has fewer bowties. A rough local argument suggests the pure matching is optimal, but I did not verify that against the source result.
